newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli finance minister warns of economic crisis.
newsitem.headline: Israeli finance minister warns of economic crisis.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Thursday the Israeli economy would plunge into crisis if parliament did not approve a 4.9 billion shekel cut in the 1997 budget.

"The 4.9 billion shekels has to be approved in its entirety. It's the minimum we need to put the economy back on a positive track," Meridor told a meeting of the Israeli Manufacturers Association in Tel Aviv.
Meridor said the budget would be sent to parliament in October and the government would agree to discuss changes in the composition of the cut but not in its size.
"If it doesn't pass, I know what kind of crisis we would sink into," he said.
The proposed cut is equivlant to 3.2 percent of spending, excluding debt servicing.
On Wednesday, the International Monetary Fund issued an interim report urging the government to accelerate passage of the budget in order to deal with the imbalance in its fiscal account.

Meridor said this year's budget deficit would total 12 billion shekels or more -- four billion shekels more than the government had targeted. He said lower than expected revenues was one problem, but government spending, especially in the area of public sector wages, was also a problem.
Meridor said there had been a 25 percent increase in real public sector wages in the last three to four years.
He said that the capital markets have also been suffering for a long time and the government must deal with this problem.
"The economy has been growing for the past six to seven years, but in the capital markets we are in a different world," Meridor said.
It was not normal, he said, that in a country where growth was so high, companies could not use the capital markets to raise money.
A government-appointed committee will issue a series of recommendations next week to deal with the crisis in the capital markets, Treasury officials said.
